name: Fast Track Design Methods
description:
WS 2024/25: AEC Hackathon
>> Lecture Information Event 13.11.2024; 12:00-13:00 // Zoom Link
>> Block Course 22.11.-24.11.2024 // Kick-Off in Room 2300@0503
>> Final Presentations 12.12.2024 // Room 2345@0503
>> https://opensource.construction/events/aec-hackathon-munich/

Discuss in an interdisciplinary three-days hackathon questions regarding the future of architecture, engineering and construction with software-based solutions. Define a concept of open source software and prototype the solution. Present your work in front of your peers and leading experts from technology, management and architecture.

The module focuses on topics of the built environment, for which interdisciplinary approaches are required and cooperation between engineering, IT, business administration and architectural disciplines is important.

The topics vary from semester to semester and are challenged in appropriate formats such as Design Sprint, Hackathon or Design Thinking Workshop. Methodologically, they include the following steps:

- Context analysis for a given subject using techniques from the fields of design, architecture, business management and IT,
- Idea generation with creativity techniques from the fields of design, architecture, business management and IT,
- Idea selection with evaluation methods from the fields of design, architecture, business management and IT,
- Prototyping with tools and methods from the fields of design, architecture, business management and IT,
- Presentation techniques from the fields of design, architecture, business management and IT.

The module examination consists of a successful participation in the block event (workshop) and a scientific elaboration of the contents achieved in the block event. The scientific elaboration (brochure, approx. 20 pages per group) will be done as an interdisciplinary group work, which has to be submitted in digital form at an appropriate distance to the block event (approx. 4-6 weeks). The elaboration will be used to assess the extent to which the students are able to develop, visualize and document results in an interdisciplinary group work in individual work steps and individual work packages. The elaboration consists of an executive summary, an in-depth description, further processing and scientific foundation of the contents elaborated in the workshop, a documentation of the block event and the group process, and a final evaluation of the block event in its suitability for promoting creativity and innovation. For the group participants, the focus of the report needs to be aligned to their respective discipline. Participating students of business administration are required to set a business focus on the above-mentioned elements. Depending on the topic, the focus of a market and environment analysis, the formulation of a business model with a simplified income / expenditure breakdown, the development of an implementation strategy with sales or networking channels for the contents must be worked out. Further business management specializations can be agreed upon in individual cases. The presentations of interim and final results during the mandatory attendance events (workshops) ensures the student’ progress in convincingly communicating their concepts to an expert audience.
